> 明夷。利艱貞。

Hexagram 36 is about a light being put out, and the word for it is more violent than the usual translation suggests.

## 夷 is 平 — to flatten

說文: 夷，平也. Original sense: level, flat.

The extension runs: 平 → 夷平 (to level) → 夷滅 (to wipe out) → 傷 (to wound).

Two steps between "level" and "wound," and both are the same act: level a thing, and it is gone; it is gone, and it is wounded.

The classic uses the third sense: 傷.

So 明夷, literally, is "the light flattened."

Not the light extinguished. The light levelled.

And flattening is worse than extinguishing. A fire put out leaves ash. A thing flattened leaves no trace at all.

## 垂其翼，三日不食

初九 明夷于飛，垂其翼。君子于行，三日不食。有攸往，主人有言.

A bird in flight whose wings hang: wounded, unable to go far.

The noble one travelling, three days without food — an approximation, meaning the extreme of hardship.

有攸往，主人有言 — and wherever he arrives, the host has something to say about it.

So the first line of the chapter is a flight with no welcome at either end, which is exactly what it means for the light to be flattened: the injured thing is also the thing nobody wants to be seen receiving.

## 左股 / 左腹

六二: wounded in the left thigh — off to one side, not the root of the body, and repairable. 用拯馬壯，吉: a strong horse to pull one out.

六四: 入于左腹，獲明夷之心，于出門庭 — entering the left side of the belly (deep, hidden), finding the heart of 明夷, and going out through the gate.

Left appears twice: once outside (the thigh), once inside (the belly). So the hexagram maps the injury from the surface inward and then back out the door.

And 獲明夷之心 is the most important phrase in the chapter: what is found at the depth of the flattening is its heart — which is to say, the light was flattened and the light knows why.

## 箕子之明夷

六五 箕子之明夷，利貞.

箕子, the 易's choice among three.

Confucius, in 論語·微子: 殷有三仁焉 — three benevolent men in Yin. 微子 left; 比干 remonstrated and was killed; 箕子, whose ruler was in chaos, feigned madness, hid his brightness, and kept his purpose without bending.

Three men, one situation, three answers: leave, die, become a slave.

The 易 chooses the one who became a slave.

Which is a hard position to defend and the hexagram defends it: 利貞 — it is beneficial to stay correct. Not to survive. To remain correct.

## 用晦而明

The 象: 君子以莅眾，用晦而明 — govern the crowd by using obscurity, and so being bright.

Not putting the clarity on the surface. Outside, thick and dim; inside, clear. Governing without the sharp-eyed inspection of everyone.

Which is the chapter's craft instruction, and it is the only one that can be practised: you cannot stop the light from being flattened, but you can decline to flatten others with your own.

## The test

Take a period when your work or your judgement was not seen. Ask which line you were on: the bird with hanging wings, the thigh, the belly, or the slave. And then ask the question the fourth line answers: at the depth of it, did you find the heart of the thing — that is, do you know why it happened?
